item.title: Ba stays top of Extra Premier League after 4-1 win over Lautoka
item.description: Ba FC has maintained its place at the top of the Extra Premier League standings after thrashing Lautoka FC 4-1 yesterday. The victory sees the Men in Black remain at the top of the table with 33 points, one point ahead of second-placed Labasa FC, who edged Navua FC 1-0.
item.content:encoded:
Ba FC has maintained its place at the top of the Extra Premier League standings after thrashing Lautoka FC 4-1 yesterday.

The victory sees the Men in Black remain at the top of the table with 33 points, one point ahead of second-placed Labasa FC, who edged Navua FC 1-0.

Rewa FC remains in third place with 29 points after playing out a 1-1 draw with Nadi FC.

Meanwhile, Nadroga FC defeated Nasinu FC 1-0, while Tailevu Naitasiri FC claimed a thrilling 3-2 win over Suva FC.

With just three rounds remaining in the Extra Premier League season, the race for the league title is heating up as teams also look to build momentum heading into one of Fiji's most prestigious football tournaments, the Extra Battle of the Giants.

Ba, Labasa, Rewa, Lautoka, Navua, Suva, Nadi and Nasinu have all secured their places in the tournament.

Nadi has bounced back strongly after missing out on the BiC Fiji FACT earlier this season to secure its place in the Battle of the Giants.

Meanwhile, Nadroga and Tailevu Naitasiri have missed out after finishing outside the top eight and will not feature in this year's tournament.

The Battle of the Giants pool matches will be played from 4th to 6th September, with the semi-finals and final scheduled for the following week at 4R Stadium, Govind Park.

item.title: Fiji to face France, Croatia and Egypt at Handball Youth World Championship this week
item.description: 12 young Fijian women are preparing to carry the nation’s hopes on the international stage as they compete at the International Handball Federation (IHF) Women’s Youth World Championship in Romania. The Fiji Under-18 girls’ handball team will make history when they take part in the global tournament, facing some of the world’s top young handball nations in the group stage.
item.content:encoded:
12 young Fijian women are preparing to carry the nation’s hopes on the international stage as they compete at the International Handball Federation (IHF) Women’s Youth World Championship in Romania.

The Fiji Under-18 girls’ handball team will make history when they take part in the global tournament, facing some of the world’s top young handball nations in the group stage.

Fiji will begin its campaign against France on Wednesday, July 29, before facing Croatia on Thursday, July 30.

The team will then complete its group-stage matches against Egypt on Saturday, August 1.

The young athletes have been working hard in preparation for the challenge and are determined to represent Fiji with pride against established handball nations.

Their journey to Romania has received a significant boost through support from the Office of the Prime Minister and the Chinese Embassy in Fiji, with funding assistance helping the team meet preparation and participation costs.

The support has been welcomed as a major contribution towards ensuring the players and officials can take part in Fiji’s first appearance at the prestigious international competition.

item.title: Anthony Joshua silences Prenga with brutal second-round knockout
item.description: Anthony Joshua overcame a dramatic first-round scare before knocking out Kristian Prenga in the second round of their heavyweight clash at the Jeddah Superdome in Saudi Arabia. The British former world champion secured the victory at the official time of 2 minutes and 43 seconds of round two in the DAZN pay-per-view main event this morning.
item.content:encoded:
Anthony Joshua overcame a dramatic first-round scare before knocking out Kristian Prenga in the second round of their heavyweight clash at the Jeddah Superdome in Saudi Arabia.

The British former world champion secured the victory at the official time of 2 minutes and 43 seconds of round two in the DAZN pay-per-view main event this morning.

Joshua found himself in trouble early as Prenga came out aggressively and landed a powerful right uppercut that appeared to stun the heavyweight. The Albanian fighter continued to apply pressure, driving Joshua back towards the ropes and forcing him to touch the canvas, resulting in a counted knockdown.

Despite the early setback, Joshua remained composed and responded in the second round. He regained control with his jab before setting up a powerful right hand that ended Prenga’s challenge and secured the knockout victory.

The win improves Joshua’s record to 29 victories, four defeats and 26 knockouts, while Prenga drops to 20-2 after entering the bout with an impressive record of 20 wins and 20 knockouts.

There were no judges’ scorecards required as Joshua stopped the contest before the end of the second round.

The victory keeps Joshua’s plans for a highly anticipated showdown with Tyson Fury later this year alive.

However, for a brief period in Jeddah, Prenga threatened to derail those plans with a fearless opening attack.

Joshua’s experience and power ultimately proved decisive, allowing him to recover from the early danger and secure another statement win in the heavyweight division. Source: DAZN/Middleeasy
